Much of the initial logs on the pad involve general maintenance work, but there are more recent ones.

<cÿÿ >Galactic Standard Rotations Ago: 103</c>
<c ÿÿ>"Always pretty boring with this work. Not enough traffic, in and out, aside from cargo. Part of me wishes I also knew more of what they're doing in this facility, but I suppose that's above my pay-grade. I get paid either way, though, so I don't much mind."</c>

<cÿÿ >Galactic Standard Rotations Ago: 99</c>
<c ÿÿ>"Been hearing some stuff about people getting sick over the last couple days. Far more than usual. I hope it's not something with the food going bad. Glad I'm not one of the live-ins here. Heard the food isn't great here, anyways."</c>

<cÿÿ >Galactic Standard Rotations Ago: 94</c>
<c ÿÿ>"I'm sorry! I'm sorry! I'm sorry! I had to do it! If I hadn't done it, those things would've gotten me, too! Please forgive me... I locked down the docking bay when I heard the screams from within. Oh stars... Those screams. Inhuman and enough to drive a man insane. I can still hear them in there. However, I only hear those things now. The screams of the other workers seems to have stopped. I suppose they're all dead. What's worse is that I tried getting out on one of the shuttles but there's some sort of tractor beam stopping escape. What the hells?! Why is there even a tractor beam installed in this facility, and why was it activated now of all times?!... Stars..."</c>

<cÿÿ >Galactic Standard Rotations Ago: 61</c>
<c ÿÿ>"Haven't made an entry in quite some time. The screams thankfully stopped a long time ago. Managed to survive this long on what little food I could find in these crates, but it's almost run out. There's probably more in the mess, but I'm not risking going in there to find out. At least I've had someone to talk to so as to keep my sanity in check. Nacks says hi, by the way. He wanted me to make sure I put that in here."</c>

<cÿÿ >Galactic Standard Rotations Ago: 55</c>
<c ÿÿ>"Wastng away. Cant do this mch longr. So littl strenth left. Nacks said hed save us, thogh. Just ned a litle more teim."</c>

<cÿÿ >Open Log. Active for 53 Galactic Standard Rotations</c>
<c ÿÿ>"nacs is usls ples don let m dddddddddddddddd</c>

The entries end there.

Among the workload of tasks on the console, there are scattered log entries as well. There is only one that stands out, however. It appears it was meant to be sent out, publicly, but failed to transmit.

<c ÿ >BEGIN VIDEO PLAYBACK</c>


<c ÿÿ>The video opens with a man with full beard and somewhat long hair. He has bags under his eyes showing a likely lack of sleep, and carries a panicked look on his face as he speaks. "I only have a moment to do this. I'm Warren Zarla, a low ranking researcher here. Something is happening here and I can't really explain what it is. People are just going crazy and attacking oth-..." He's cut off by the sounds of horrifying screams in the distance, looking back quickly to check for something, then looks back at the screen. "To whoever finds this message, please show it to appropriate authorities. I don't have much time left." He then looks more directly at the camera and forces a smile. "Taryn... Daddy loves you very much. But I have to go now... I love you." The feed is then shut off.</c>

<c ? >TRANSMISSION BLOCKED. TRY AGAIN? Y/N</c>

Much of the datapad seems to just contain various simple games and porn vids. There is a single log entry, though.

<cÿÿ >Galactic Standard Rotations Ago: 93</c>
<c ÿÿ>"Right. Just gonna log this down in case things go bad. It's been about a day since I heard those crazy screams from somewhere. No one is telling me anything as not even the guard has come to check on me since it happened. But lucky me, the force field has been on the fritz. If I can just slip the datapad in front of the scanner during one of the flickering periods, I should be able to get myself out of here. I need something to eat. But hey. Before I do that, I'm Greer Wills. I was put in here for a couple days due to trying to feel up one of the secretaries. Begged to not get terminated from my job as its the only one I've got. I guess I should be thankful to Czerka for just putting me in here as a lesson, and let me keep my job. But anyways, looks like it's about time. Gotta go!"</c>

The log ends there.

Much of the datapad is just general logs on disciplinary action and reasoning for the brief stays by troublemakers.

<cÿÿ >Galactic Standard Rotations Ago: 96</c>
<c ÿÿ>"Not surprised to see Greer in here. I mean, I'm surprised he wasn't just relieved of his job. But I suppose Czerka can be lenient at times in regards to that. I guess that's why we have this small detention area, anyways. But yeah. He's always made weird passes at the women here. I guess actually touching was what finally did him in. Just wish he had more than a few days in here."</c>

<cÿÿ >Galactic Standard Rotations Ago: 94</c>
<c ÿÿ>"This is gonna be very quick. I heard weird screams from further in the facility. Inputting this to remind myself to make a report later. Anyways, time to go check it out."</c>

There are plenty of older entries in this datapad, but most are more professional logs of visitors. There are very few personal logs.

<cÿÿ >Galactic Standard Rotations Ago: 100</c>
<c ÿÿ>"Been seeing an odd upswing in people getting sick around the station. Haven't really been feeling it myself, but Verem had to go to the medbay because of how bad it was getting. Maybe one of the guys off station picked something up, or maybe there's a leak in some fuel pipe. Who knows? You'd think Czerka would pay to get something like that fixed, though."</c>

<cÿÿ >Galactic Standard Rotations Ago: 94. Voice Log.</c>
<c ÿÿ>Heavy breathing is heard from what sounds like a woman. "Oh Stars... What was that?..." A loud, horrifying scream is heard echoing from somewhere distant in the facility, immediately followed by more screams in a sort of symphony. The woman screams in panic, and others in the room can be heard babbling in their panic. "What the-...? The door is locked down! What the hells! LET US OUT!" Banging is heard on metal by multiple people as panic seems to spread in their voices. A door is heard sliding open from somewhere nearby and the woman along with the others start screaming in fear. The screams are immediately followed by the same horrific screams from earlier, except this time from very close by. One last scream can be heard from the woman before the recording cuts out.</c>

No further entries.

This datapad mostly consists of general data regarding maintenance. There are a few personal entries, however.

<cÿÿ >Galactic Standard Rotations Ago: 103</c>
<c ÿÿ>"I really don't write in this much. Not a lot goes on in this place, though. Eat, work, sleep, repeat. Phil is just covering my break at the moment. I just wish there was something more exciting that would happen in here. I mean, there are the science personnel that work up on the development level, but that's a restricted area to anyone else. Kinda feels like one of those old vids I watched as a kid. But this is real life. I dunno. I'm just rambling at least. I should get back to work, though."</c>

<cÿÿ >Galactic Standard Rotations Ago: 95</c>
<c ÿÿ>"Been seeing people getting sick. Not sure what would be causing it, but I guess it's... something? I did wish for something exciting to happen. I mean, it's not exactly exciting, but at least something is actually /happening/ around here."</c>

Most of the entries are data and logs regarding generator maintenance, but there are a few personal logs.

<cÿÿ >Galactic Standard Rotations Ago: 97</c>
<c ÿÿ>"So, I don't really care what anyone says about it being boring around here. I get enough excitement with my job. Maybe I just enjoy what I do, though. These old generators are always having issues, though. It's definitely my job to make sure things don't overload or something worse."</c>

<cÿÿ >Galactic Standard Rotations Ago: 95</c>
<c ÿÿ>"Woke up this morning not feeling all that great, but what else is new? Plenty of others are getting sick from this bug going around. Not surprised I'm getting sick, too. People are saying I need to go to the medbay, but I gotta keep working on all this. It's just some sniffles and a cough, anyways. I'm fine."</c>

There are no newer entries.
This datapad is covered in blood and too broken to make any use of.

The readout shows information regarding the lavatory lockdown.

<cÿ  >LOCKDOWN IN EFFECT

HULL BREACH DETECTED WITHIN LAVATORY</c>

The message repeats.

The datapad is fairly damaged, but there is a part of a voice log that can be extracted from it.

<c ÿÿ>"Blasted hells! They're getting in!" A man's voice is heard in a panicked tone as continual sounds of metal being banged on can be heard in the background. Another man's voice is heard from the side. "I almost got this thing rigged up and we can get out past them!" The first man then speaks again. "Are you sure the explosion won't kill us along with /them/?!" Mixed in with the banging on metal, there is a brief sound of a hand slapping a couple times on metal, before the other man speaks. "Can't be sure, but trust me. We just gotta open the door and toss it at them." The first man speaks again in a hesitant tone. "Alright. I'll get the door, then." Footsteps are heard before the sound of buttons being pressed. "Th-..."</c>

The rest of the recording appears to be corrupted.

The readout shows information regarding the lockdown.

<cÿ  >MANUAL OVERRIDE | LOCKDOWN IN EFFECT</c>

The message repeats.

Value.value: As you neared the station, whether willing or not, the station seemed almost to pull you in on its own. Despite your best efforts to disengage, it became obvious you were trapped in a tractor beam. Looking around now, the docking area is very dark and cold, and you can make out shadows of other ships, equipment, and other assorted objects strewn about. There is an unpleasant odor of decay lingering in the air, and seems to become worse as you move further in. Whatever happened here, it's now obvious that you have no choice but to check it out.

The unpleasant odor you smelled on entry gets stronger as you wander through the darkness. You now realize where the smell is coming from. A partially decaying corpse can be made out through the dark, laying on a bedroll with various cargo and junk scattered about him. Beside him is a lone datapad.

The hall seems to split, here. To the left and right, it seems to continue for a short way before seemingly stopping, with closed doors. Looking forward down the hall ahead, it just seems to keep going into the darkness.

Entering through the door, you notice it's a bit more open again. Through the darkness, various objects like tables and chairs thrown about. Each of the small open rooms also carry very faint glows from something within, perhaps indicating the last vestiges of power in the station. Whatever happened here, though, people left in a hurry. Or tried to.

Likely some sort of break area, the chairs are thrown about as if the people sitting in them or moving past them were in a great hurry. More pools of the sticky crimson can be seen about in large and small quantities, but still you see no actual bodies.

Entering through the door, you notice it's a bit more open again. Through the darkness, various objects like tables and chairs thrown about. Each of the small open rooms also carry very faint glows from something within, perhaps indicating the last vestiges of power in the station. Whatever happened here, though, people left in a hurry. Or tried to.

Entering through the door, you notice it's a bit more open again. Through the darkness, various objects like tables and chairs thrown about. Each of the small open rooms also carry very faint glows from something within, perhaps indicating the last vestiges of power in the station. Whatever happened here, though, people left in a hurry. Or tried to.

The area here appears to have been some sort of condensed office space. Various desks are lined up in rows, likely meant for the lower waged workers, as well as open doorways letting a faint glow of whatever clinges to life through the remaining power, stream through. The coppery smell of blood lingers heavily in this room, as well, overtaking most of your senses.

Moving further in from the docking bay, you enter what appears to be a reception area. Some basic appointment terminals next to the doorway behind you give a faint glow in the darkness as you look about the area. Waiting areas to either side that are a regular sight in such a room, as well as various advertisements, artwork, and the easily recognizeable symbols on the far wall, indicating the Czerka Corporation. But there is something immediately off, you notice, as you take a step into something wet. Upon looking down, you now notice the sticky crimson blood all over the floor, as if something was completely drained of it in some violent manner. But even with all the blood, there's one thought that you can't get out of your mind: Where are the bodies?

The area here appears to have been some sort of condensed office space. Various desks are lined up in rows, likely meant for the lower waged workers, as well as open doorways letting a faint glow of whatever clinges to life through the remaining power, stream through. The coppery smell of blood lingers heavily in this room, as well, overtaking most of your senses.

The area here appears to have been some sort of condensed office space. Various desks are lined up in rows, likely meant for the lower waged workers, as well as open doorways letting a faint glow of whatever clinges to life through the remaining power, stream through. The coppery smell of blood lingers heavily in this room, as well, overtaking most of your senses.

Among all the scattered office areas, this one appears to stand out through the sheer level of violence that likely happened. It's as if whoever was inside had tried to barricade the open doorway with as much as he could get his hands on, inside. However, whatever entered pushed it all aside and likely led to their death. That said, despite the blood caking the floor and walls in here, there is no sign of a body.

Based on the appearance of it, the door here seems to be for an elevator. However, for the moment, no matter what you seem to do, it won't open. Checking the terminal next to it, it appears to require level 4 clearance or higher.

As your round the corner, you seem to enter the cafeteria. Old and rotting food lingers on the tables and by the kitchen, likely having been there for quite some time. There are definitely signs of struggle, like the rest of the station, but perhaps just a bit less so here.

Hungry? Well, it looks like you'll have to figure something out later. The food stands before you appear half empty, but what little remains appears to be perishable and assails your sense of smell with a barrage of decay.

As the rest of this hellish station, there appeared to be a large struggle in here. What you can immediately tell is that this was the workers quarters and that there were efforts made to barricade the door with tables, couches, beds, and chairs. However, given the blood throughout the area, whatever they were trying to keep out... got in.

Immediately upon moving through the door, you realize this is some sort of security checkpoint. Three doors can be seen ahead, though all but the rightmost one is closed. Or mostly closed. THe door on the left appears to have tried closing, but got stuck halfway through a body of a man who appeared to be in a rush. The old blood and strong smell of decay spreads through the area.

Moving through the open door, you seem to enter one side of some sort of security station. To the left, force fields still remain up, surrounding what appears to be the entrance to a sealed off docking shaft, perhaps for larger vessels docking to the station. Through to the other side, you can't make out much of anything, save for the very faint outlines of desks and the blinking lights of terminal buttons. Turning back around to the right, now, you see much the same here. Desks laid about, control terminals, and otherwise, as well as a door terminal blinking through the darkness on the far wall.
Through the door is another security checkpoint with desks on either side of a scanner. Beyond it is a security door leading further in.

Beyond the security door, it's very dark. The only real light aside from whatever you carry on you comes from what little light is given off from the stars outside a window on the far wall. As you make your way further in, however, it becomes obvious this is one of the station's cargo holds.

The generator room becomes obvious the moment you open the doors. While still no better in terms of light compared to the rest of the facility, you can still hear the faint hum of something working. Perhaps some sort of backup power. While you may have hoped not to find more in here, you once again notice a lot of blood, as well as some sort of trail moving around one of the generator parts.

You come across a guard station of some sort, serving as an entryway to a holding area. The door is closed leading further in, but to the left is an obvious guard booth to keep an eye on those coming in and out.
As expected from the previous room, you enter a small holding area with a few small cells, likely meant for troublemakers or something else. A curious thing to have in a space station like this.

Approaching one of the cells, the first thing you noticed is a pool of blood and a severed arm holding a datapad just outside of the flickering force field. Given the status of the force field, it's very possible the arm was severed in an idiotic attempt to escape.

The smell that hits you as you enter the room reminds you of nothing other than a medical center. Purifying fluids, kolto, blood, and other smells all at once. But the one that stands out, is the stinking smell of rot.

Finally, the rotting smell is explained as you come across a pile of what could only be seen as rotting meat in a pool of old blood. It hits you harder than any other smell in the room, and you feel like gagging. It's hard to tell what it might have been once, but the sight of a half-eaten human skull likely makes it obvious. There are other bodies seen at the corners of the room, but this one gives off the worst of it.
